title: Initial input-position update rule
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine, let $w$ be a binary input, and let $p\in\mathbb N$ and a finite list of bits $l$ be given. If the first bit of $l$ is true, its second bit records whether $p=1$, its input-symbol bits encode the symbol at position $p$ in $w$, and its designated chain bits encode the presence and value of the time-zero input-chain value at $p-1$ when $p>0$ (and are absent when $p=0$), then the local input-position update rule applied to $l$ yields the encoding of whether the time-zero input head is at $p$ and of the time-zero input-chain value at $p$.
hypotheses_covered: second list bit equals the indicator of p=1
input-symbol presence and value bits encode the input symbol at p
chain presence and value bits encode the time-zero chain at p−1, or are absent when p=0
